novel_features.name: One-shot report export
novel_features.description: Export a Power BI or paginated report to PDF/PPTX/PNG/XLSX/CSV/DOCX with a single command — POST, poll, and download handled internally.
novel_features.rationale: Every competitor exposes the three async steps (POST ExportTo, GET status, GET file) separately. Users hand-roll the poll loop.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when an agent needs a Power BI report as a file (for OCR, attachment, or visual analysis). One call instead of three plus a poll loop.

novel_features.name: Saved DAX query catalog
novel_features.description: Save named DAX queries to a local catalog and re-run them by name. Parameterize with --var key=value.
novel_features.rationale: Requires a local SQLite store that no competing CLI maintains. pbicli accepts inline DAX only — no query library, no parameters, no reuse.
novel_features.example: powerbi-pp-cli dax save monthly-revenue 'EVALUATE SUMMARIZECOLUMNS(Dates[Month], "Revenue", [Total Revenue])' && powerbi-pp-cli dax run monthly-revenue --group W --dataset D --csv
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when iterating on DAX with an agent — save once, refine, re-run by name instead of re-pasting the query each turn.

novel_features.name: Refresh failure dashboard
novel_features.description: Surface every dataset whose most recent refresh failed in the last N days, with error messages.
novel_features.rationale: Requires the local catalog of datasets plus a per-dataset refresh-history fetch — no single Power BI endpoint returns this; admin APIs aggregate but require admin scope.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use for the 'what broke since yesterday' question. Joins local catalog + live refresh history; admin scope not required.

novel_features.name: DAX from file with CSV out
novel_features.description: Read a DAX query from a file and emit CSV — pipe-friendly for downstream tooling.
novel_features.rationale: pbicli execute outputs JSON only. Users hand-roll jq pipelines to flatten.
novel_features.example: powerbi-pp-cli dax run --file query.dax --group W --dataset D --csv > out.csv
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when a DAX query is long enough that shell quoting is painful, or when downstream tooling wants tabular input.

novel_features.name: Auth doctor with tenant settings explainer
novel_features.description: Decode the AAD token, show tenant/app/scopes/expiry, probe /groups, and explain which Power BI tenant setting is blocking you if the probe fails.
novel_features.rationale: Power BI has 5 common auth failure modes (token expired, wrong scope, tenant setting disabled, SP not in workspace, RLS blocking). This command names which one is biting.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when 'it returned 401/403' but you don't know why. Generic doctor commands probe network; this one decodes the JWT and explains the failure class.

novel_features.name: Dataset schema introspection
novel_features.description: Best-effort tables/columns/measures listing for a dataset. Tries INFO.TABLES() DAX (Premium), falls back to dataset metadata.
novel_features.rationale: Microsoft's Remote MCP knows the model schema internally but doesn't expose it programmatically. pbicli has no equivalent.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use before writing a DAX query to know table and column names. Reduces 'EVALUATE [guessed table name]' trial-and-error.

novel_features.name: Device-code + service-principal login built in
novel_features.description: Interactive device-code flow by default (no Azure CLI needed); service-principal client_credentials flow when --client-secret is passed. Token cached and refreshed.
novel_features.rationale: pbicli depends on `az` being installed for token acquisition. We do both AAD flows natively so anyone with a Microsoft account can use the CLI without external tooling.
novel_features.example:
powerbi-pp-cli auth login                    # device code, opens browser
powerbi-pp-cli auth login --tenant T --client-id C --client-secret S    # service principal
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use the no-arg form for personal use; pass --client-secret in CI or headless agents. Tokens cached at ~/.config/powerbi-pp-cli/token.json with refresh-on-expiry.

narrative.headline: Pull data from the Microsoft Power BI REST API for analysis in Claude — every read-only feature pbicli has, plus saved DAX queries, one-shot report export, and a local SQLite catalog no Power BI tool has.
narrative.value_prop: Read-only Power BI CLI optimized for AI agents. Execute DAX queries with --csv and --select, export reports to PDF in a single command, browse workspaces/datasets/reports offline via the local catalog, and surface refresh failures across your tenant without admin scope.
narrative.auth_narrative: Power BI auth is OAuth2 against Azure AD. Two paths: (1) bring your own bearer token via the POWERBI_TOKEN env var (get one with `az account get-access-token --resource https://analysis.windows.net/powerbi/api`), or (2) `powerbi-pp-cli auth login --tenant T --client-id C --client-secret S` to exchange a service principal for a token (cached locally, refreshed when expired). The `auth doctor` command decodes your token and explains which of the five common failure modes is biting if requests are being denied.

quickstart.comment: Sign in to Power BI via device-code flow. Opens a browser tab to verify; persists a bearer token to ~/.config/powerbi-pp-cli/config.toml.
List workspaces, narrowing to id+name so the agent context stays small
List datasets in a specific workspace (this is the example workspace ID from your URL)
See the tables/columns of a dataset so you know what to query

quickstart.command: powerbi-pp-cli dax run --query 'EVALUATE TOPN(100, Sales)' --group 804c5edc-6653-4149-8d08-a11279824b7a --dataset DATASET_ID --csv
quickstart.comment: Run a DAX query against the dataset and emit CSV
Export the report from the URL you provided to PDF in one command

troubleshoots.fix: Run `powerbi-pp-cli auth doctor`. Most often: the AAD app is not added to the workspace as a member, or the tenant setting 'Allow service principals to use Power BI APIs' is off.

troubleshoots.symptom: DAX query returns 'More than 100,000 rows in a query result'
troubleshoots.fix: Wrap the EVALUATE in TOPN or add a date filter. The 100K row / 1M value / 15MB hard caps are server-side per the executeQueries API contract.

troubleshoots.symptom: DAX query returns 429 Too Many Requests
troubleshoots.fix: 120 queries-per-minute-per-user limit applies regardless of dataset. Back off and retry after the Retry-After window.

troubleshoots.symptom: Bearer token expired (401 after a working session)
troubleshoots.fix: Re-run `powerbi-pp-cli auth login` if using service-principal mode, or refresh `POWERBI_TOKEN` from `az account get-access-token` (tokens last ~1 hour).

troubleshoots.symptom: Service principal getting 401 on a dataset that works for users
troubleshoots.fix: Service principals are not supported on datasets with RLS enabled or SSO/live-connect to on-prem Azure Analysis Services. Use a delegated-user token for those.

narrative.when_to_use: Use when an agent needs to pull data out of Power BI for analysis in Claude — running DAX queries against semantic models, exporting report pages as PDFs, or browsing the workspace/dataset/report hierarchy to find the right resource ID. Read-only — no model authoring, no admin operations, no embed-token issuance. Pair with a Power BI workspace where you've added either a service principal or your AAD user as a member.

recipes.title: Pull a slice of report data as CSV for spreadsheet analysis
recipes.command: powerbi-pp-cli dax run --query 'EVALUATE TOPN(1000, FactSales)' --group W --dataset D --csv > sales.csv
recipes.explanation: DAX EVALUATE returns rows; --csv flattens the executeQueries JSON into columns suitable for spreadsheets or pandas.

recipes.title: Find a workspace by fuzzy name across hundreds
recipes.explanation: After a separate sync, search runs offline FTS so finding the right workspace ID takes one command instead of paginated list calls.

recipes.title: Narrow a deeply-nested response to the fields the agent actually needs
recipes.explanation: Power BI list responses return ~20 fields per row including embedUrl, createdBy, modifiedBy. --select with dotted paths drops the rest — typical 5x reduction in agent context bytes.

recipes.title: Export a specific report page as PDF
recipes.command: powerbi-pp-cli report-export REPORT_ID --group W --format PDF --output report.pdf --wait
recipes.explanation: POST then poll then download in one command. --wait blocks until the export succeeds; pass --wait=false to get the export ID and poll later.

recipes.title: Find datasets that failed to refresh this week
recipes.explanation: Iterates every accessible workspace and dataset, pulls each one's most recent refresh history record, returns only the failing ones with error messages.
